documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 34F.

The year: term vaginal delivery 2/2024; second pregnancy found to have fetal spina bifida/Chiari II at 18 weeks, then fetal demise at 19 weeks with D&E 10/2024. She says the winter has been better than she feared. Psychiatry down to monthly again, sertraline 50. PHQ-9 4, GAD-7 4.

Migraine: 2-3 a month, sumatriptan effective, no ED trips for headache. RLS: well controlled on pramipexole 0.125, no daytime symptoms. Abdominal ache: 'background noise,' some weeks none.

Not actively trying for pregnancy but not preventing either. Continues prenatal vitamin. Cycles have always run irregular.

Preventive: Pap/HPV due 2026. Flu and COVID done this fall. Tdap 12/2023. Lipids and HIV/HCV done 2022. Exercise: walks the stroller most days. Seatbelt, smoke detectors yes. Feels safe at home.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. HEENT, neck, thyroid normal. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. Extremities without edema. Skin no concerning lesions. Neuro nonfocal. Mood and affect normal.

A/P
1. Health maintenance. CBC, CMP, TSH today.
2. MDD, somatic symptom disorder: stable, continue sertraline and psychiatry.
3. Migraine without aura: stable on rescue therapy.
4. RLS: stable.
RTC 6 months for med check, 1 year physical.

events.reason: Left lower abdominal pain and vaginal spotting

reports.text:
Indication: positive pregnancy test, left lower quadrant pain, spotting. LMP about 6 weeks ago.
Technique: transabdominal and transvaginal grayscale and color Doppler imaging.
Findings: The uterus is anteverted and normal in size. The endometrial cavity is empty; no gestational sac, yolk sac or fetal pole. No intrauterine pregnancy. A complex mass is seen in the left adnexa, separate from the left ovary. The right ovary and right adnexa are normal.
reports.conclusion: No intrauterine pregnancy. Complex left adnexal mass. In the setting of a positive pregnancy test, ectopic pregnancy is a consideration; correlate with serial hCG.

reports.text:
Specimens: (A) endometrial curettings; (B) left fallopian tube, salpingectomy.
Gross: (A) scant tan-red tissue. (B) segment of fallopian tube with a hemorrhagic, disrupted wall.
Microscopic: (A) decidualized endometrium; no chorionic villi or trophoblast identified. (B) chorionic villi and trophoblast within the tubal lumen and wall with hemorrhage and wall disruption.
reports.conclusion: A: Decidualized endometrium, no products of conception. B: Left fallopian tube with ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN NOTE
Date of visit: 05/20/2025

CC: left lower abdominal pain.

HPI: 34 y/o G3P1011 with sudden, sharp left lower abdominal pain that started about 6 hours before arrival. Light vaginal spotting for the past 2 days. LMP about 6 weeks ago; cycles irregular. Pregnancy in 2024. Treated for PID about three years ago. Sexually active with one partner, inconsistent condom use.

PMH: migraine, depression, restless legs, somatic symptom disorder. PSH: D&E 10/2024. Meds: sertraline 50 mg, pramipexole 0.125 mg, prenatal vitamin, sumatriptan prn. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 110/70, HR 98, T 37.2 C (99.0 F). Uncomfortable. Abdomen: tender in the left lower quadrant with rebound. Pelvic: os closed, no active bleeding, cervical motion tenderness.

Data: urine hCG positive. Serum quantitative beta-hCG 1500 mIU/mL. CBC unremarkable. Transvaginal ultrasound: empty uterus, no IUP, complex left adnexal mass.

MDM: pregnancy of unknown location with a complex left adnexal mass; ectopic pregnancy is the main concern. Hemodynamically stable. Gynecology consulted and admits for serial hCG and further evaluation.

Disposition: admitted to gynecology.

documents.title: Gynecology Discharge Summary
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
GYNECOLOGY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 05/20/2025 via the ED  Discharged: 05/23/2025

Admitting diagnosis: pregnancy of unknown location, complex left adnexal mass.
Discharge diagnosis: ruptured left tubal ectopic pregnancy, status post left salpingectomy.

Course: Admitted for observation and serial beta-hCG. hCG 1500 mIU/mL on 05/20 and 1800 mIU/mL on 05/22, an abnormal rise over 48 hours. On 05/22 she underwent diagnostic dilation and curettage; no products of conception were seen on the specimen. She was taken for laparoscopy the same day, which found a ruptured left tubal ectopic pregnancy, and a laparoscopic left salpingectomy was performed. Right tube appeared normal. Postoperative course uncomplicated; tolerating diet, ambulating, pain controlled with oral analgesics. Pathology: decidualized endometrium without villi; left tube with ruptured tubal ectopic pregnancy.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge medications: resume home medications (sertraline 50 mg daily, pramipexole 0.125 mg nightly, prenatal vitamin daily, sumatriptan 50 mg as needed).
Instructions: no lifting over 10 lb for 2 weeks; pelvic rest 2 weeks. Gynecology post-op visit in 2 weeks. Follow up with primary care.

Gynecology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-hospital follow-up. Admitted 5/20-5/23 for a left tubal ectopic: hCG 1500 -> 1800 over 48 h, D&C without products of conception, then laparoscopy found it ruptured and the left tube was removed. ED, discharge summary and path reviewed.

Feels much better. Port sites a little sore, no fever, bleeding light and tapering. Gyn post-op check next week. Off school since the 20th, back Monday for the last weeks of the year.

Mood: 'another hit, but I'm steadier than in the fall.' PHQ-9 5. Psychiatry aware. Sertraline 50, no changes.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well appearing. Three laparoscopic port sites clean, dry, healing, no erythema. Abdomen soft, mildly tender near the umbilical port only.

A/P
1. S/p left salpingectomy for ruptured ectopic, recovering well. Ectopic resolved. Gyn follow-up as planned; contraception and future pregnancy planning with gyn.
2. MDD: stable.
3. Return-to-work note given for 6/9.
Med check in August.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refills requested: sertraline 50 mg #90, sumatriptan 50 mg #9, pramipexole 0.125 mg #90. Last OV 6/4/25, missed 8/20 med check, rebooking. Pended to PCP. -- Sent all three, 90-day supplies, sumatriptan with 2 refills.

documents.title: News
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Positive test again. LMP Sept 3. After May I'm terrified it's in the wrong place again. The gyn office is getting me an early ultrasound Friday. Still on everything the same. Can I get my flu shot while I'm pregnant again?

documents.title: RE: News
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Congratulations, and I completely understand the fear. The early ultrasound is exactly the right step; let me know what it shows. Yes to the flu shot, and the updated COVID shot too. The nurses can do both whenever you can get in. Same plan on your medications as the last pregnancies.

documents.title: RE: RE: News
documents.author: patient
documents.body: It's in the uterus!!! Heartbeat and everything. Booking the shots for next Friday.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: 6 weeks pregnant. Screening negative, no prior vaccine reactions. Trivalent flu IM L deltoid and updated COVID mRNA IM R deltoid. VIS provided for both. Waited 15 min without issue.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request: prenatal vitamin with folic acid, 1 daily, #90. Pt is 11 weeks, followed by OB. Pended to PCP. -- Sent with 3 refills.
